title: Fix Drag Child Piece Output Design Center
description:
When dragging a child piece (e.g. only `t_f1_b_c1`) in the Drag storybook, the diff output is correct (shows connection update) but the DESIGN_OUTPUT window shows an identical copy of the input — the piece doesn't visually move.

Root cause: `dragPiecesInDesign` for child pieces only produces a `ConnectionDiff` (updating `connection.u/v`). The diagram renders piece positions using `piece.center`. In a flat design, child piece centers are set during flatten. When the connection offset is updated, the piece center is NOT updated, so the output diagram shows the same positions.

Also: for root pieces, the algorithm sets `diff.center = { u: offset.u, v: offset.v }` which REPLACES center with the offset value. `applyPieceDiff` does a replacement (not additive). This is wrong for root pieces at non-zero centers.

Fix:
1. In `dragPiecesInDesign` (semio/js/index.ts): 
   - Root pieces: look up current center and set `diff.center = { u: center.u + offset.u, v: center.v + offset.v }`
   - Child pieces: if piece has center set (flat design), also add a piece center update with new absolute center (current + offset), in addition to the connection diff
2. Update test data `diff.design.semio.json` so root piece center diffs use absolute new center (current + offset), not just the offset
3. Update the Nakagin test "produces only connection diff" → now also expects piece center update for the flat child piece
summary: Adjusted the Nakagin diff fixture so the tambour is no longer encoded as a removed piece. Connection 4e90d5ab-6f49-4ecb-a527-7b240353fbe0 now carries the relationship change via connections.updated with parent 357c1d20-f0ce-4da7-b6d7-feb4a0e42eb9, and semio/ui regression coverage now verifies that a parent-connection update keeps the child piece in the scene instead of delete/add churn. Verified with semio/js and semio/ui Vitest runs.
